we have developed a fast-growing embryogenic callus from Nakasousyu, and that this callus is useful for producing regenerable suspension cultures and for obtaining fertile plants from wheat protoplasts.
Nakasoushu, an early maturing, small grain wheat variety, was regenerated from its protoplasts, and that the protocol was applicable to other wheat varieties, including the Australian wheat Bodallin.
the Japanese wheat cultivars Nakasoushu, Norin 61, and Norin 61-3 were successfully regenerated from protoplasts.

the development of an efficient system for the production of protoplasts from wheat suspension cultures.
the isolation of protoplasts from suspension cultures of Nakasoushu, a fast-growing Japanese wheat cultivar, and Bodallin, an Australian cultivar, which is characterized by its high yield.
the development of a fast-growing, small granular embryogenic callus and its application to protoplast culture.

the use of nurse cells, the use of an osmoticum, and the use of 2,4-dibromophenoxyacetyl methyl (BAP) in the culture medium were important for the successful induction of Nakasoushu wheat protoplasts.

the use of nurse cells and protoplast isolation from embryogenic calli are essential to obtain a high frequency of division and regeneration in wheat protoplasts.
